extracted.intended_audience: people suffering from nervous breakdowns ("nerves"), their families, and general readers seeking dietary/lifestyle cures
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, prescriptive regimen (dietary, drinking, eating habits, exercise, and behavioral) intended to prevent and cure functional nervous disorders / neurasthenia through long-term changes in how and what a person eats and lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chew all solid food to the consistency of cream
rubrics_metrics.description: You must chew all food until it is of the consistency of cream (Fletcherizing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make this a lifelong habit; do it at every meal and as part of a combined regimen. Chewing thoroughly aids digestion, prevents intestinal toxemia and gas, increases mental and physical endurance, and often leads to weight loss that should not be feared. Doing this practice alone is often insufficient — it must be paired with other measures (exercise, proper food choices, drinking habits). If you can't take enough time for full mastication, better to go hungry than bolt food.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sip all liquids slowly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not gulp drinks; sipping slowly helps digestion and avoids distress. In particular, avoid drinking during the meal (see related rule); if you need a drink after eating, take it slowly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not drink during meals; prefer hot water
rubrics_metrics.description: The victim of 'nerves' should never drink during the meal but after it, if he must drink anything at all; plain hot water is best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drink a cup of plain hot water half an hour before breakfast and a cup after meals if desired. Cold water (a pint or more) should be drunk between meals daily. Avoid tea and coffee (see separate rule). Hot water before breakfast is recommended even if you skip the meal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eat sparingly — quit before you are full
rubrics_metrics.description: You should always quit eating while you still feel you would like a little more — eat sparingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the feeling of wanting a little more as a guide. Overeating leads to dilated stomachs, intestinal toxemia, and the recurring depressions seen in nervous people. Eating slowly and chewing well naturally reduces intake. Persist in the habit; initial weight loss is expected and acceptable for improved health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take sufficient time for meals (eat slowly; allocate time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give proper time to eating; ideally take an hour for a meal (devote three of twelve daily hours to three meals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you travel and must eat in eating-houses, take simple food (bread-and-butter sandwiches) and eat them slowly. Do not let social impatience or others' derision cause you to abandon slow eating. Regularly allocating time reduces bolting and enforces mindful chewing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid bolting food / rapid eating
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not bolt your food or rush through meals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bolting causes digestive disturbance, gas, and absorption of poisons leading to mental depression. Compare to a thirsty horse that drinks too fast; humans likewise harm themselves by rapid eating. Train yourself to chew every mouthful to cream; if you cannot, better to abstain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid tea and coffee
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual afflicted with 'nerves' has no business drinking either tea or coffee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute plain hot water. Tea and coffee are discouraged for nervous sufferers because they aggravate the condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid commercial sugar, eggs, and animal food for 'offspring of nervous parents'
rubrics_metrics.description: People who are the offspring of nervous parents and who have had a nervous breakdown should not eat commercial sugar, eggs, or animal food of any kind whatever.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author presents this as a strong dietary prohibition for those predisposed to or suffering from nervous breakdowns; it is part of the 'right and wrong diet' recommended and should be followed strictly as described later in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine dietary changes with physical exercise and mental activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Diet alone will not cure 'nerves' — the cure must come through common sense exerted along several related avenues: proper nutrition, physical exercise, and mental activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid idleness (e.g., rocking in an armchair); outdoor life and exercise are necessary (see chapter IV). The benefit of diet is largely nullified without bodily exertion and intellectual/mental engagement. Use a multi-pronged, persistent approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persist patiently and maintain regimen long-term
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have patience and persist in the regimen; do not quit the treatment before nature has had time to do her work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improvements may require months or years; temporary trials (e.g., chewing alone for a short time) do not prove ineffectiveness. Many sufferers prematurely abandon measures when they see weight loss or slow progress — the author urges steadfastness and lifelong adherence to beneficial habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'rest cures' as sole treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Rest cures at sanitariums may give temporary benefit but do not permanently cure nervous cases when used alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanitariums often fail to remove the underlying physical causes (dietary and digestive) that produce 'nerves.' Rest may help temporarily, but for a lasting cure you must combine diet, chewing, drinking rules, exercise, and other measures described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid intoxicants (alcohol, tobacco) and cravings for harmful foods
rubrics_metrics.description: Nervous people often crave foods (sweets, chocolates) that hurt them; overeating creates a 'food drunk' akin to alcohol debauch; avoid alcohol and tobacco.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craving does not equal need; refrain from foods and substances that produce temporary stimulus followed by severe depression. The analogy to alcohol emphasizes that repeated overeating maintains toxic states that perpetuate nervous illness.

rubrics_metrics.name: If possible, get household cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: When a nervous person in a household adopts the regimen, it is desirable that other household members join in the practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spouses or family members who adopt slow chewing and sparing eating often benefit themselves. Household-wide adoption removes social pressure, supports the patient, and improves overall family health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chew acid fruits thoroughly to avoid distress
rubrics_metrics.description: People who say they cannot eat acid fruits because of distress should chew an apple, pear, or other fruit to a cream to avoid trouble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper mastication prevents gas and distress from fresh fruits. If chewing alone does not help, follow the detailed diet recommendations given elsewhere in the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not fear impending insanity
rubrics_metrics.description: The sufferer need not fear that nervous breakdowns will lead to insanity; this disease is a functional nervous trouble and not insanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harboring the fear of going insane slows recovery. Reassurance that insanity is unlikely is part of the psychological guidance: reducing fear aids progress and adherence to regimen.
